_comment: The compiled form of doc/permission-policy.md — the cases already enumerated.
Every entry is a permission decision, so every entry is read by a human before it merges:
the promotion path is /permission-promote -> a kanban card -> card-reviewer -> gate -> PR.
Nothing writes into this file at runtime; the broker only reads it. Runtime verdicts land
in ~/.spo-perm/provisional/, which is the queue this file is fed from.
The seed below grants NO permission that policy §6 does not already grant: every entry is
read-only, and §6 already allows a read-only call when the arbiter cannot answer. What the
seed adds is the `guidance` — the corrected form that rides back to the caller on an allow
(policy §4bis), so the lesson costs a file read instead of a model call from the very first
capture. Anything that is not read-only is deliberately absent: it belongs to the arbiter
The domain is inside the key on purpose — see permission-broker.js, signature().

rules.reason: Reading a file changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 (read-only) and §6.
rules.guidance: The Read tool is the sanctioned form here (CLAUDE.md § Environment): it needs no permission, reports line numbers you can cite, and reads the ISO-8859 .pas files of SPO-Original correctly — where shell `cat` and `grep` silently return nothing.

rules.reason: A search changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 (read-only) and §6.
rules.guidance: Prefer the Grep tool (pattern/path/glob): no permission, no word-splitting on paths containing spaces, and correct on the ISO-8859 files. If this search touches ~/SPO-Original or ~/SPO-ASP, the shell form is refused outright by legacy-search-guard — a false negative there feeds a wrong kind/arity into rdo-members.ts.

rules.reason: Listing paths changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 (read-only) and §6.
rules.guidance: The Glob tool is the sanctioned form (pattern + path). Shell `find` piped into `xargs` word-splits on `Interface Server/` and dies on the apostrophe in `Pastel's mp3/` — measured: 2 files reported out of 15.

rules.reason: A `sed` without -i only reads. Allowed by policy §1 (read-only) and §6.
rules.guidance: Use Read with offset/limit to read a range, and Edit to change one. `sed -i` is a write and is classified as such — it never reaches this rule.

rules.reason: Reading the end of a file changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 and §6.
rules.guidance: If this is the tail of a verdict log, `npm run verdict -- <alias> [--tail=N]` is the one-call sanctioned form: it keeps the real exit code, writes the full log under ~/.spo-bench/logs/ and prints EXIT=<code> last. A pipe onto a verdict command reports the pipe's exit code, not the command's.

rules.reason: Reading the start of a file changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 and §6.
rules.guidance: Same as tail: `npm run verdict -- <alias>` for a verdict, Read with limit for a file. `| head` on a search destroys the exit code — grep's exit 2 becomes the pipeline's 0, so an error reads as an empty result.

rules.reason: Counting changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 (read-only) and §6.
Probing a file's type changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 and §6.
rules.guidance: This is the sanctioned way to confirm the ISO-8859 encoding trap before concluding a symbol is absent from SPO-Original (CLAUDE.md ⚠).

rules.reason: Comparing two files changes neither. Allowed by policy §1 and §6.
Reading metadata changes nothing. Allowed by policy §1 and §6.
